title: Co-Parenting Self-Assessment
subtitle: A private reflection to help you identify strengths, growth areas, and the next child-focused step.
how_to_use: Answer based on how co-parenting is working right now, not how you hope it will work. This is a reflection tool — not a diagnosis or custody evaluation.
disclaimer: This is a reflection tool — not a diagnosis or custody evaluation.

sections.label: Child-Focused Parenting
questions: I can separate my feelings about the other parent from decisions about our child.
I keep our child out of adult disagreements and avoid using the child as a messenger.
I can identify our child's current emotional, educational, medical, and developmental needs.
I support our child's relationship with the other parent when it is safe and appropriate.
I try to make parenting decisions based on what helps our child feel secure and supported.

sections.label: Communication
questions: I can communicate about our child without unnecessary criticism, blame, or personal attacks.
I share important information about school, health, activities, and schedules in a timely way.
I can keep messages brief, informative, respectful, and focused on the child when conflict is high.
I can listen for the other parent's concern even when I disagree with the proposed solution.
I use a communication method that reduces confusion and creates a useful record when needed.

sections.label: Reliability, Routines & Transitions
questions: I follow the parenting schedule and give reasonable notice when a change is needed.
I help our child move between homes without placing the child in the middle of tension.
I can maintain predictable routines while allowing reasonable flexibility when appropriate.
I make sure our child has needed school, medical, activity, and personal items for transitions.
I address transition problems directly with the other parent or an appropriate professional.

sections.label: Decision-Making & Information Sharing
questions: I understand which parenting decisions require consultation or joint decision-making.
I provide the other parent access to important records and information when appropriate.
I can discuss options before taking a fixed position on an important parenting issue.
I can identify areas where we already agree or have similar goals for our child.
When we disagree, I can focus on the specific decision rather than reopening unrelated past disputes.

sections.label: Conflict Management & Boundaries
questions: I recognize situations that tend to trigger conflict between us.
I can pause before responding when a message or event makes me angry or defensive.
I maintain appropriate boundaries and avoid monitoring or controlling the other parent's household.
I know when structured communication, mediation, therapy, or another resource may help.
I can use a conflict-resolution process instead of repeatedly arguing about the same issue.

sections.label: Alignment & Readiness
questions: I can name at least three goals I believe both parents may share for our child.
I can distinguish between an essential child need and a personal preference.
I am willing to consider more than one workable option for resolving a parenting issue.
I can describe what is going well in our co-parenting relationship, even if some areas are difficult.
I am prepared to build a child-focused Foundation Statement and identify next steps.

tiers.title: 96–120 · Strong co-parenting practices
tiers.body: Protect these strengths while addressing remaining issues.

tiers.title: 76–95 · Workable with growth areas
tiers.body: Focus on lowest sections and create specific decision structures.

tiers.title: 56–75 · Significant structure helpful
tiers.body: Consider structured communication and child-focused mediation.

tiers.title: 30–55 · High difficulty reported
tiers.body: Prioritize safety, structure, and professional review.
